title: VWP Evidence
description: An evidence reference: a source record supporting facts and claims. May point to a package-local file (path) or an external system (externalRef).

path.description: Forward-slash relative path to a package-local evidence file.

externalRef.description: A reference to a record held outside the package. 'locator' is a free-form string; set 'locatorType' to declare how to interpret it, and 'retrieval' to describe how (and with what auth) a long-lived URL is fetched.

locatorType.description: How to interpret 'locator'. 'url' triggers URI validation and enables the 'retrieval' block; 'path' is a filesystem/relative path; 'vwp-ref' is a cross-package reference (e.g. other.vwp#objectId); 'opaque' is any other identifier (docket, ticket, S3 key).

retrieval.description: How to retrieve this reference over the network. Metadata only: the package never carries the secret needed to actually authenticate.

url.description: Absolute URL to fetch. Should be long-lived/stable for referenced evidence.

auth.description: How a retriever authenticates. Aligned to RFC 6750 (Bearer token usage) and RFC 9728 (OAuth 2.0 protected-resource metadata discovery).

scheme.description: Auth scheme. 'bearer' (RFC 6750) and 'none' are defined; other non-empty strings are permitted for forward compatibility and interpreted by the retriever.

tokenHint.description: WHERE the retriever obtains the credential — never the credential itself. Use a source scheme such as 'env:VAR_NAME', 'vault:path/to/secret', 'oauth:client-id', 'keychain:item', or 'prompt:label'. A literal secret here is a validation failure.

discovery.description: RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata URL (typically '<origin>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource'), from which a retriever learns the authorization server, supported token types, and required scopes.

scopes.description: OAuth scopes a retriever must request to access this resource.

contentHash.description: SHA-256 the retrieved bytes are expected to match. Turns a live long-lived URL into verifiable evidence: an online retriever fetches, hashes, and compares.

retrievedSnapshotAt.description: When the bytes behind 'contentHash' were last retrieved and hashed.

derivedFrom.description: Evidence id this object was mechanically derived from (e.g. a text extraction of a PDF, an OCR of a screenshot). The original remains the authoritative source; the derived layer exists so facts can anchor into verifiable text.

transform.description: How the derived evidence was produced from its source. Required in spirit whenever derivedFrom is set, so the derivation is reproducible and challengeable.
